title: Strong Kadison–Kastler stability
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: The proof, after OpenAI's 2026 papers, that close von Neumann algebras are conjugate by a unitary near the identity, with a tolerance that depends only on the required closeness: for every eps > 0 there is delta(eps) > 0 such that unital von Neumann algebras M, N on any Hilbert space with d(M, N) < delta(eps) satisfy uMu* = N for a unitary with ||u - I|| < eps. Finite factors are treated with boundary means of countable groups, measurable cocycles, double ergodicity, common tracial position and Jordan maps; infinite factors with a fixed tensor factor of type III_1, rescaled Tomita graphs, infinitesimal normalizers of type III factors, frequency nests and analytic multipliers, a common modular action and common crossed products; general algebras with Dixmier's approximation theorem, the central decomposition and separable tests. Two counterexamples complete the picture: close separable C*-algebras that are not unitarily conjugate, from convergent sequences, a relative tensor norm and a deformation of the free group's regular representation; and one-sided near inclusions without small spatial embeddings, from a circle family of representations and Voiculescu's almost commuting matrices.
prerequisites: Foundations of von Neumann algebras: operator topologies and the double commutant theorem, Kaplansky's density theorem, the continuous and Borel functional calculus, the weak compactness of the unit ball of B(H), projections and types, normality of *-isomorphisms, completely positive maps, Polish spaces and measurable selection, derivations of von Neumann algebras, traces on finite factors (course Foundations of von Neumann algebras, OA-FND-BI-06, OA-FND-KD-07, OA-FND-CF-07, OA-FND-CF-11, OA-FND-LT-10, OA-FND-TY-03, OA-FND-TY-17, OA-FND-WA-18, OA-FND-WA-19, OA-FND-PB-09, OA-FND-PB-11, OA-FND-INNER-THEOREM; supplement OA-FND-TA-11, OA-FND-TA-12)

Arveson's distance formula 2 dist(x, A') = ||ad x|_A||_cb and the uniform commutator estimate (course Kadison's similarity problem: Completely bounded homomorphisms and similarity, Corollary 4.5; The uniform commutator estimate, Theorem 3.1)

Traces and noncommutative integration: the commutation theorem, trace-preserving conditional expectations, commutants of semifinite algebras, minimal projections (course Traces and noncommutative integration)
Spatial tensor products of von Neumann algebras: matrix units, slice maps and the commutation theorem (course Tensor products of operator algebras)
Haar measure on compact groups (course Harmonic analysis on locally compact groups, OA-FND-HM-05)

Injective von Neumann algebras and the uniqueness of the injective II_1 factor (course Injective factors); an injective subalgebra with the same core commutant (course Relative bicentralizers and core commutants)

Tomita-Takesaki theory, the standard form, the modular expectation theorem and the continuous core (courses OA-MOD and OA-FLOW); ultraproducts of type III factors (course Type III factors); Stone's theorem (course Analytic elements, strips and KMS); the central decomposition (course Measurable fields and direct integrals)

open_obligations: N1 Christensen's theorem on injective near inclusions: if R is injective and R is nearly included in Q within gamma < 1/100, there is a unitary v in the von Neumann algebra generated by R and Q with vRv* in Q and ||v - I|| <= 150 gamma; with the reverse near inclusion and gamma < 1/101, vRv* = Q (J. Cameron, E. Christensen, A. M. Sinclair, R. R. Smith, S. White, A. D. Wiggins, Kadison-Kastler stable factors, Duke Math. J. 163 (2014), Theorem 3.3(i), after E. Christensen, Near inclusions of C*-algebras, Acta Math. 144 (1980); free: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4116v3). Stated in lesson 2, Theorem 3.1; used in lessons 7, 8, 14 and 16. Intended home: a course on perturbations of injective von Neumann algebras (not yet in the programme).

N2 Ricard-Roydor: an associative bilinear map m on a von Neumann algebra P with ||m - m_P||_cb <= 1/11 has a completely bounded linear bijection L with L(m(x, y)) = L(x)L(y) and ||L - id||_cb <= 10 ||m - m_P||_cb, adjoint preserving when m(x*, y*) = m(y, x)* (E. Ricard, J. Roydor, A noncommutative Amir-Cambern theorem for von Neumann algebras and nuclear C*-algebras, J. Funct. Anal. 267 (2014), Proposition 3.2 in arXiv version 2; free: https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.1970v2). Stated in lesson 2, Theorem 3.2; used in the completely positive criterion (lesson 2, Proposition 4.1) and through it in lessons 12, 14, 15 and 17. Intended home: a lesson on Hochschild cohomology and perturbations of products (not yet in the programme).

N3 Common tracial position: close II_1 factors M, N with separable preduals, mutually nearly included within 0 < g < 1.74 x 10^-13 and sharing an injective subalgebra R with R' n M in R, have faithful normal representations in common standard tracial position that agree on R, within beta < 50948 sqrt(g), with the four properties of lesson 6, Proposition 1.2 (Cameron, Christensen, Sinclair, Smith, White, Wiggins, Lemma 4.10 in arXiv version 3; free: https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.4116v3). Stated in lesson 6, Proposition 1.2; used in lesson 7, Theorem 2.1. Intended home: a lesson on standard tracial position of close II_1 factors (not yet in the programme).

N4 Sakai's theorem: every derivation of a simple unital C*-algebra is inner (S. Sakai, Derivations of simple C*-algebras. II, Bull. Soc. Math. France 99 (1971), 259-263; free: https://www.numdam.org/articles/10.24033/bsmf.1719/). Stated in lesson 10, Theorem 0.1; used in lesson 10, Lemma 2.1, the uniform infinitesimal estimate. Intended home: a lesson on derivations of C*-algebras (not yet in the programme).
